Let
\[
t=\frac{\mu}{\rho}.
\]
Since \(\mu\in[1,4]\), choosing \(\rho\) is the same as choosing an interval
\[
t\in[a,4a],\qquad a=\frac1\rho>0.
\]

For a fixed \(t\),
\[
P_{f_\mu,\rho}=(I+tQ)^{-1},\qquad P_{g_\mu,\rho}=(I+tR)^{-1}.
\]
Writing
\[
\alpha=\frac1{1+t},\qquad \beta=\frac1{1+4t},
\]
we have
\[
F=(I+tQ)^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&0\\0&\beta\end{bmatrix},
\]
and, because \(R\) has eigenvalues \(1,4\) in the \((1,1)\), \((1,-1)\) directions,
\[
G=(I+tR)^{-1}
=\frac12\begin{bmatrix}\alpha+\beta&\alpha-\beta\\
\alpha-\beta&\alpha+\beta
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The Douglas-Rachford step is linear:
\[
z^+=T_{\theta}(t)z,\qquad 
T_{\theta}(t)=I+\theta\bigl(G(2F-I)-F\bigr).
\]

A direct simplification gives the minimax optimum at
\[
a=\frac14,\qquad \theta=2,
\]
so
\[
\rho=4,\qquad t\in\left[\frac14,1\right].
\]
For \(\theta=2\), the endpoint matrices are
\[
T_2\!\left(\frac14\right)
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\frac9{50}&0\\[2mm]
\frac9{50}&0
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
T_2(1)
=
\begin{bmatrix}
0&-\frac9{50}\\[2mm]
0&\frac9{50}
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Both have Euclidean operator norm
\[
\frac9{50}\sqrt{2}.
\]
For \(t\in[1/4,1]\), the largest singular value of \(T_2(t)\) is bounded above by the same value; equivalently,
\[
T_2(t)^TT_2(t)\preceq \frac{81}{1250}I.
\]
The determinant/minor check reduces to polynomials with nonnegative Bernstein coefficients on \([1/4,1]\), with equality only at the two endpoints.

Conversely, for any interval \([a,4a]\) and any \(0<\theta\le2\), the endpoint singular-value inequalities force
\[
\sup_{t\in[a,4a]}\|T_\theta(t)\|_2\ge \frac9{50}\sqrt2,
\]
with equality only when
\[
a=\frac14,\qquad \theta=2.
\]
Thus \(\rho=1/a=4\), and the minimizing pair is unique.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{(\rho_*,\theta_*,\mathcal C_*)=\left(4,\,2,\,\frac{9\sqrt2}{50}\right)}.
\]
